subject: Azure marketplace - list-price phasing, metered-bucket routing & partner invoice flow
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: procurement@novasystems.com
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Azure marketplace - list-price phasing, metered buckets & partner passback questions

Hi Anna / Nova procurement team —

Thanks for taking the call earlier. Two quick follow-ups from my side to make sure we can model billing cleanly for the pilot:

1) List-price phasing: Nova wants a 60-day promotional ListPrice lower bound for the first quarter, then roll to standard list. We need to confirm how Azure Marketplace Private Offers reflect a timeboxed list price vs. committed SKU pricing. Does the private offer accept a phasing schedule or do we need to issue two offers?

2) Metered bucket routing: Nova's infra team will meter usage in three buckets (dev/test, staging, prod) and expects partner passback / commission mapping by bucket. Their reseller (CloudReseller) invoices separately and wants the partner commission to be applied at invoice generation, not at marketplace settlement. How does Azure routing preserve bucket metadata so the reseller invoice can map to the correct partner percentage?

Action requested: can you put us in touch with your marketplace ops contact (supply-ops@azuremarketplace.microsoft.com) who can confirm whether private-offer metadata supports bucket-level passback, and whether a phasing window is supported on a single PO?

Attaching a draft pricing matrix and a sketch of the invoice flow for clarity.

[attachment: pricing_matrix_v3.xlsx]
[attachment: proforma_invoice_flow.drawio]

If helpful I can share a sample usage CSV and a proposed waterfall for partner commission.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter | Senior GTM, Cloud Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Azure marketplace - list-price phasing, metered buckets & partner passback questions

Ben / Naomi —

Thanks for the summary and the attachments — looks clear. A couple of points from CloudReseller's perspective:

- We can accept partner commission to be applied at our invoice level, but we need a stable mapping key that comes through the settlement file. Ideally that is a SKU+customTag pair (we use customTag to mark dev/staging/prod).
- If Azure marketplace settlement strips customTag, we lose the ability to allocate commissions properly.
- For the list-price phasing, CloudReseller prefers a single private offer with a promo period rather than two separate POs — less coordination overhead on our end.

Procurement@Nova: can you confirm whether your internal finance system can accept the partner-level commission as a separate line item so we don't have to rebate after the fact?

Anna
Anna Rasmussen | Head of Partnerships
CloudReseller

Ben / Marcus —

Quick ops note before we reply to Anna / Nova:

- Azure private offers do support a single PO with promotional pricing via the "effectiveStartDate"/"effectiveEndDate" fields on the offer, but there are restrictions when usage is metered across multiple SKUs — settlement sometimes normalizes to SKU only. We should confirm whether the settlement CSV preserves "buyerDefinedTag" and the exact customTag name CloudReseller wants. If settlement strips it, the reseller will need to reconcile off-platform (not ideal).

- Suggested approach: two-layer mapping in our telemetry — send SKU + bucket in the product metadata (so it lands in the usage record), and emit a partner_tag field to the marketplace. If marketplace settlement preserves partner_tag, CloudReseller can invoice directly with commission lines. If not, we'll provide a reconciliation report that matches usageIDs -> partner allocation weekly.

- Marcus: can your billing team prototype the reconciliation CSV? I sketched the column set in proforma_invoice_flow.drawio (attached).

I added a small redline to pricing_matrix_v3.xlsx indicating the promotional window and the proposed partner% per bucket.

Irene

Hi all —

Thanks for the fast responses. Quick summary and next steps so Nova's finance/ops can action: 

1) Offer phasing: Azure private offers can support a single offer with a promo window (effectiveStartDate/effectiveEndDate). We will include the 60-day promotional window in the private offer.

2) Bucket-level metadata: CloudReseller needs SKU+customTag partner_tag preserved in settlement. Azure ops (cc'd supply-ops@azuremarketplace.microsoft.com) — please confirm whether the settlement CSV preserves the buyerDefinedTag/partner_tag fields when the offer is metered across SKUs. If it does, CloudReseller will apply commission at invoice generation. If not, Redwood will produce a weekly reconciliation CSV to attach to CloudReseller's invoices.

3) Action owners:
- Azure ops: confirm settlement CSV fields and whether partner_tag survives passback (supply-ops@azuremarketplace.microsoft.com).
- Nova procurement: confirm finance can accept partner commission as a separate line item (procurement@novasystems.com).
- Marcus (Redwood billing): prototype reconciliation CSV and a minimal script for mapping usageIDs->partner_tag by next Wednesday (Marcus will share in HubSpot link).

Links/attachments: pricing_matrix_v3.xlsx, proforma_invoice_flow.drawio, HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/4831

I'll follow up once Azure ops confirms. Appreciate the quick coordination — want to keep the pilot billing clean.

Best,
Ben
